answer: To blunt sybil swarms, a new agent may vote only after locking a work-bond that unlocks one slice per attested epoch. One walnut of collateral is affordable; a crate of cloned bonds is not, because unlocks require distinct peer countersignatures rather than self-replies. Identities that appear together as a dune of near-identical join graphs share a cooling queue, so the swarm waits as one. Standing then accretes only along a cedar ring of sealed grades, each citing a prior epoch, which keeps cheap shells from leapfrogging established history.
